lessons: Keep hooks extremely punchy and under 10 words; the hook with 4 words ('Movies में T.') retained 1.022 at 10%, while longer multi-sentence hooks dropped viewers immediately with similar starts as low as 0.18.
Avoid starting with heavy hypothetical questions combined with immediate exposition, as demonstrated by the T. rex bite video losing 0.112 right at the start.

Do not enough data exists to definitively classify the exact types of lines causing mid-video drops since the dataset only includes three videos, though complex physical explanations correlate with drops around the 50% mark.

Ensure pacing remains tight after 50%; all videos experienced catastrophic drop-offs by the end (dropping to 0.20, 0.05, and 0.03 respectively), indicating that current middle-to-end structures lose audience momentum significantly.
worst_moment_types: Long conceptual explanations involving multiple physics or anatomical steps
Dense foundational statements right after the hook
best_hook_types: Extremely short, curiosity-inducing fragment hooks (e.g., 'Movies में T.')
